AfterRoomEntered.issue: Rollup of guard N1 per binding rule 4. SlingOfCourage.cs:21-28 applies PowerVar<StrengthPower>(2) from AfterRoomEntered when `room.RoomType == RoomType.Elite`, and for a CombatRoom that hook fires after CombatManager.SetUpCombat and BEFORE Hook.BeforeCombatStart (CombatRoom.cs:225-229) -- so C# guarantees the +2 Strength is on the player before ANY combat-start listener runs. The sim re-hosts the effect one dispatch point later, inside the on_combat_start pass, in relic-registration order. The room-type gate and the constant are faithful (guards N2, N3); the SLOT is a dormant gap (N1), which this entry carries as its rollup. The re-hosting itself is forced -- the sim's own after_room_entered hook (relics/base.py:194, dispatched at run.py:983) runs before any CombatState exists and so cannot hold a power -- and it is the same re-hosting relics/girya.py:22 applies to the identical C# hook; audits/relic/girya.json guard G2 verdicts that mechanism a DORMANT gap and binding rule 3 pins this entry to the same verdict rather than letting it soften to a divergence. guards.what: N1 (DORMANT gap, matching audits/relic/girya.json G2): the slot move -- C# guarantees the Strength lands BEFORE every BeforeCombatStart listener; the sim puts it INSIDE that pass
guards.issue: MECHANISM: for a CombatRoom, `Hook.AfterRoomEntered` fires at CombatRoom.cs:228, between SetUpCombat (line 225) and AfterCombatRoomLoaded (line 230), which starts the combat and dispatches Hook.BeforeCombatStart. So in C# nothing in the combat-start pass can see a player without the +2. In the sim the relic IS a combat-start listener, so whether another listener sees the Strength depends on relic-acquisition order. This is exactly audits/relic/girya.json guard G2 -- the SAME C# hook re-hosted the SAME way -- and it is cited and matched rather than re-derived (binding rule 3); girya's G2 already names sling_of_courage.py:27 in its own dormancy evidence, so the two records agree by construction. REACHABILITY (DORMANT), re-executed here for this relic's own effect (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b14.py sling): a grep of every `def on_combat_start` body under sts2_rl/relics/ for a power READ (`powers.get` / `powers[`) returns NONE -- the 23 implementers apply Thorns/Plating/Dexterity/Strength, heal, add a potion, upgrade draw-pile cards, mark cards Ethereal, or reset their own counters, and Strength addition is commutative so no ordering changes the final amount. Porting any combat-start effect that READS player Strength, or any monster whose opening intent is computed from it, makes it live -- and it would go live at girya's site simultaneously, so this is a two-site fix. Rule 7: relics/girya.py, audits/relic/girya.json, audits/relic/anchor.json and CombatRoom.cs are not hashed here.

guards.rationale: The sim's CombatState.room_type is the run-layer RoomType the combat happens in, set by RunState.create_combat's caller and None for room-less combats (combat.py:96-101). EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py sling): ELITE gives Strength 2 and MONSTER, BOSS and None all give 0 -- so a boss fight grants nothing, matching C# (RoomType.Boss is a distinct value). The two formulations cover the same set: C# fires the hook for every room and filters to Elite; the sim only ever asks in a combat and filters the same way, and a non-combat Elite room does not exist. guards.what: N5: Flash() (SlingOfCourage.cs:25), CanonicalVars (line 17), ExtraHoverTips (line 19) and the ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext (line 26)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CheckIfUsedUp's status write / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Title / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, the localized name, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext is the multiplayer choice-synchronisation handle used where no player prompt can occur (it throws if one is requested), which is exactly the sim's situation -- PowerCmd.apply never prompts.
